newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wedesday July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wedesday July 30.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday met with unions and employers to close the first round of welfare reform talks before the summer break. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, finance minister Vincenzo Visco and labour minister Tiziano Treu also attended the meeting with representatives of 31 groups, including employers' body Confindustria and Italy's three main unions (all).
* Sergio Cofferati, head of Italy's largest union CGIL, said progress had been made in welfare reform talks and a union-backed solution was possible when talks are due to resume in the autumn (all).
* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers' federation Confindustria, said talks aimed at introducing a reform to the country's welfare state were not moving forward and they were a waste of time (all).
* The upper house of parliament (Senate) approved on Tuesday a bill paving way for the privatisation of state telecoms group Telecom Italia.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi warned that recent turbulance in the currency makets might have a knock-on impact on European interest rates (all).

* A report by national statistic institute ISTAT showed Italian wage inflation stood at an annual rate of 4.6 percent in June compared with 4.7 percent in May and 4.1 percent in June 1996 (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Investment bank IMI said its net profits rose to 276 billion lire in the first half of 1997, up some 16 percent from 239 billion lire in the same period last year (all).
* A survey by state-funded economic research institute ISCO showed Italian industry saw a jump in orders in June with companies reporting growing optimism for the months ahead (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
